item.title: Gaza ceasefire talks end in Cairo with plans to resume next week
item.description: A two-day round of Gaza ceasefire negotiations in Cairo concluded on Friday in what sources described as a "positive atmosphere," with all parties agreeing to resume discussions in the Egyptian capital next week. The talks brought together a Hamas delegation led by Gaza chief Khalil al-Hayya, representatives of Palestinian factions, Egyptian officials, and international mediators from Qatar and Turkey.

item.title: Hamas accuses Israel of fabricating threats to justify Gaza ceasefire violations
item.description: Israeli forces carried out fresh attacks across the Gaza Strip on Saturday, with gunfire, artillery shelling, and drone activity reported in multiple areas, according to Palestinian medical sources and eyewitnesses. The violence marks yet another day of hostilities in the nearly six-month-old ceasefire that has failed to bring lasting calm to the besieged territory.

item.title: Ukraine halts Russian steel plant supplying tank factory
item.description: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on April 4 that a recent strike on the Kirovske airfield in Russian-occupied Crimea destroyed one Inokhodets (Orion) drone and damaged three others, while defense forces struck railway convoys carrying fuel to Russian troops in occupied Luhansk Oblast on April 3 and overnight April 3-4.

item.title: Oil tops $112 as economists warn Iran war risks global recession
item.description: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink has warned that crude oil prices could surge to $150 per barrel and cause a "global recession" if Iran continues to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, even after the current US-Israel military campaign concludes. The warning comes as WTI crude surged past $111 per barrel in early April trading, with Brent crude climbing above $112, amid fresh fears of escalation in the five-week-old conflict.

item.title: China ramps up Iran war diplomacy as U.S. stays on sidelines
item.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran grinds into its second month with no end in sight, China and Pakistan have emerged as the conflict's most active peace brokers, launching a joint diplomatic offensive that includes a five-point ceasefire proposal, a campaign to block the use of force at the United Nations, and a web of back-channel communications connecting Washington and Tehran.

item.title: Oil past $112 a barrel deepens Asia's currency crisis
item.description: A toxic combination of surging oil prices, a strengthening U.S. dollar, and the ongoing Iran conflict is battering currencies across Asia, with the Philippine peso and other regional units falling to record or near-record lows as the region's heavy dependence on imported energy amplifies the pain.

item.title: Hezbollah claims 38 operations in 24 hours as war with Israel escalates
item.description: Hezbollah carried out 38 military operations against Israeli forces and settlements within a single 24-hour period ending Friday, April 3, marking one of the group's most intense days of combat since the war with Israel began on March 2. The barrage of rocket salvos, drone strikes, guided missiles, and sniper fire hit targets across northern Israel and southern Lebanon, as the broader multi-front conflict involving Iran and Yemen continued to escalate.

item.title: Beijing warns Japan of 'heavier price' amid Taiwan row
item.description: China imposed sanctions on Japanese lawmaker Keiji Furuya over his repeated visits to Taiwan, freezing his assets and barring him from entering mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau, in a move that has deepened a diplomatic rift between Beijing and Tokyo.

item.title: Erdogan pushes ceasefire diplomacy on Middle East, Ukraine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke by phone on Friday, jointly calling for an immediate ceasefire in the Middle East as the conflict triggered by U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran continues to destabilize the region and rattle global markets.

item.title: U.N. Security Council postpones vote on Strait of Hormuz resolution to next week
item.description: The United Nations Security Council has postponed a vote on a Bahrain-backed resolution to secure the Strait of Hormuz, with the measure now pushed to next week after France, Russia, and China objected to language authorizing military force to reopen the waterway Iran has effectively blocked since the start of the U.S.-Israel war on February 28.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine trade deadly strikes as Zelenskyy meets Erdogan
item.description: A Russian drone struck a market in the frontline Ukrainian city of Nikopol on Saturday morning, killing five people and wounding at least 19 others, as waves of overnight aerial attacks battered the country. The violence unfolded as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Istanbul for talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan focused on the war and prospects for a ceasefire.

item.title: Iran, Hezbollah, Houthis hit Israel in coordinated Saturday assault
item.description: Israel came under coordinated fire from multiple fronts on Saturday, with Hezbollah launching a barrage of rocket, missile, and drone attacks on northern Israel and Israeli troop positions in southern Lebanon, while Iran and Yemen's Houthis simultaneously struck the Tel Aviv metropolitan area, leaving one person lightly injured and causing widespread damage.

item.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Crude oil prices vaulted past $110 per barrel this week after President Trump's primetime address on the Iran war dashed hopes of a near-term ceasefire and signaled weeks of intensified strikes ahead, deepening a global energy crisis triggered by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Israel readying strikes on Iran's energy sites, awaits US approval
item.description: Israel is preparing to attack Iranian energy facilities but is waiting for approval from the United States, a senior Israeli defense official said on Saturday, adding that any such strikes would likely come within the next week. The disclosure marks a potential new phase in the five-week-old war, shifting the focus from military and nuclear targets to Iran's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Iran threatens 'crushing' strikes on US, Israeli assets across Middle East
item.description: Iran's armed forces on Saturday issued their most sweeping threat yet in the five-week-old war, warning that any further US strikes on Iranian infrastructure would be met with "sustained and destructive" attacks on all American and Israeli assets across the Middle East. The escalation came as Tehran rejected a US-backed 48-hour ceasefire proposal, leaving diplomatic efforts in disarray.

item.title: Artemis II crew battles toilet troubles halfway to moon
item.description: The four astronauts aboard NASA's Artemis II mission have been dealing with recurring toilet troubles as they cruise toward the moon, including a frozen vent line that blocked the spacecraft's ability to dump wastewater overboard and a mysterious burning smell emanating from the bathroom area.

item.title: WHO warns of humanitarian crisis as Iran hospitals come under attack
item.description: The World Health Organization has verified more than 20 attacks on healthcare facilities in Iran since March 1, as U.S.-Israeli military operations continue to strike civilian medical infrastructure across the country. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the escalating campaign is crippling the delivery of health services and endangering patients, health workers, and civilians.

item.title: Artemis II crew prepares for Monday lunar flyby
item.description:
Four astronauts are hurtling toward the Moon aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft, now more than halfway through the first crewed lunar voyage in over half a century. The Artemis II mission, which launched on Wednesday, April 1, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, is set to carry its crew around the far side of the Moon on Monday before returning to Earth for a splashdown off San Diego on April 10.

Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen are traveling aboard the Orion capsule, which they named Integrity. On Saturday, their fourth day in space, the crew prepared for the lunar flyby while the spacecraft continued its coast toward the Moon.

item.title: Iran vows permanent control of Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran is moving to cement lasting authority over the Strait of Hormuz, advancing legislation and building a de facto toll system that analysts say is designed to outlast the current war with the United States and Israel and give Tehran a permanent lever over the global economy.

item.title: Iran cluster bombs wound 6 in central Israel as war enters sixth week
item.description: Iran fired several salvos of ballistic missiles at Israel on Saturday, causing extensive damage to homes across the Tel Aviv metropolitan area and wounding six people, as the war that began February 28 entered its sixth week with no signs of easing across the broader Middle East.
